newsitem.title: HAITI: Haiti policeman killed as riots resume.
newsitem.headline: Haiti policeman killed as riots resume.

text.p: Angry mobs burned cars and tires in the streets of the Haitian capital on Friday as a dispute between students and striking teachers flared into a second day of rioting.
Businesses closed and downtown Port-au-Prince residents fled the area as the rioters hurled rocks at vehicles and people.
About 80 police were deployed in an effort to restore order, but by noon EDT (1600 GMT) smaller riots were springing up in other areas of the city including the downtown slum of La Saline.
After a day of unrest on the streets of the capital on Thursday, a police officer was gunned down overnight and another was injured, police said.
Alix Cadet, 25, was killed when unknown attackers shot him six times not far from his home. Another off-duty officer who was with him was shot in the foot.
Port-au-Prince police chief Lionel Trecyl said: "The killing did not take place during the riots, but is the result of criminals taking advantage of the situation of general disorder."

The rioting was triggered by student demonstrations that began earlier in the week. Teachers who have not been paid by the government in some 14 months went on strike, closing schools just before final exams.

Angry students took over a downtown school on Thursday and began throwing rocks at passers-by. When police moved in and injured some students, hundreds of people began to riot, smashing windscreens and setting the courthouse, vehicles and tires on fire.
Five people were seriously injured, two by police bullets.
Education Minister Jacques Eduard Alexi called for a dialogue among teachers, students and the government to find a solution to the crisis.
"Together we can see what we can do," he said.
Prime Minister Rosny Smarth, interviewed by Haitian Radio Metropole in Chile, said he was working seriously on the problem.
"That the children are suffering is a shame. We need to find a way out of this."
Smarth said earlier in the week that this year's Haitian budget, which was recently approved by parliament, does not include money to pay the teachers the amount they are owed.
